title: The Crazy-to-Be
subtitle: There's no time to mourn the past.

items.text: Assembly Room, Polymer Exhibition Hall
Noise and chaos fill the exhibition hall again—as P-3 and the Twins deal with their escalating situation.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: That's another one of them that's gone barking mad! What the hell is going on?

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: A little help here? Hold his legs down!

items.speaker: Left & Right
items.text: Affirmative.

items.speaker: Scientist III
items.text: Let me, let me go! Ah!

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: How many does that make so far?

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Based solely on our observations, this is the seventh individual to experience a serious psychiatric break.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Crispy critters! Left, are there any sedatives we can use on 'em? Think the repair vendor could synthesize some?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: The repair vendor has experienced ... a serious emotional malfunction, Comrade Major.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Dammit! You mean that crazy fridge can't even repair herself?
P-3 jumps down from the platform, wiping away beads of sweat that now cover his forehead.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Phew! At least we tied him down. Thanks, ladies.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Wouldn't have expected these brainiacs to be so tough. It'd be easier if they are robots. All they need is a bullet to the head.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Comrade Major, please be mindful of your choice of words. There are international experts present. We should not need to remind you of your mission.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Avoiding a scandal by killing every possible witness could be an interpretation of our mission parameters.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Can it, Glove. You know that's not what I meant.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Situation's looking bleak, though: we've already got seven of these lunatics, and there's no telling if or when the rest of this crowd are gonna join them.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Plus, we still have to find those spy kids and figure out why that Belyash went rogue.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Oh yeah. That reminds me: how'd your investigation pan out, Right?

items.speaker: Right
items.text: I have cross-referenced our visitor logs with the official invitee list. Besides the supposed young doctors, there was another mismatched record—a journalist.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: What's that sound?

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Warning: large heat signature detected.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: The hell?

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Identifying machine code—MA-9 Belyash.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: That the one that switched itself on?
A huge shadow is cast over the broken glass of the assembly shop, in the middle of which lie several red dots that seemingly imply danger.
As the airtight door opens, the Twins extend their claws, and P-3 raises his shotgun, scanning for a target.
The massive shadow lumbers into the light.

items.speaker: Belyash
items.text: "Whoa, please don't hurt me."
The Belyash speaks as it raises its hands into the air.

items.speaker: Belyash
items.text: "Please listen—"

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Huh?
The once-again powered-down Belyash lies huddled in the corner as Left approaches to inspect it.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: You're saying this "Maxim" guy is behind the attack?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's right. The files we found and the access logs from the Belyash should prove it.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: What do you think about that, Glove?

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Allow me a moment, Major.
Suspending the files in the air above its tentacles, the glove scans through the documents page by page.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Analysis complete. There are two unauthorized access logs in the MA-9's database.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: The access exploit used is materially similar to the one we found in NORA's log.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: But there is a newer entry, and it appears that the second hacker has left a program behind that I am unable to parse.

items.speaker: X
items.text: That would be me, haha. It's a patented and highly classified coding language. I'd advise against removing it for now; otherwise, Maxim might regain control.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Lookie here. This seems to be a record of how our guy broke into the network. Any clue if it's the same one they used to crack the database?
P-3 hands one of the files over to Left.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Affirmative.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: It is reasonable to conclude that Maxim is responsible for the malfunctions affecting NORA, the VOV-A6, and this MA-9 Belyash.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: And therefore, that he is also responsible for the wider attack on the exhibition hall.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: If our foreign friends are correct, that may only be part of his plans. According to these files, he may also have tampered with the THOUGHT Devices.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: So, what's he aiming at?
Char-les turns another page in the air as he answers the question.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: His already-demonstrated sophistication with robotics suggests he could have easily adapted the THOUGHT Device. To start with, he is likely using his own device to control the facility's robots remotely, but ...

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: It's only logical to conclude his aim was to bring about an international uproar to disrupt the launch of Kollektiv 2.0.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If that's the case, could he also have something to do with what's happening to the scientists?

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: A reasonable hypothesis, to be certain.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Crispy critters, we've jabbered enough. Let's just find this asshole and beat the truth out of him! Do we know his location, ladies?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: There have not been any registered Turbine departures since the beginning of the attack. We can infer that the suspect is still somewhere within the confines of this platform.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If he's still here, then he must have intended to observe things from a secure location.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is there a room in this facility where you might be able to monitor the entire exhibition center—somewhere secure?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Excluding offline locations. Analyzing security and monitoring feasibility. Conclusion: the Power Control Room.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do we have some way to check if he's there?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Affirmative, provided the communication system linking these locations is not damaged.
Left attempts to contact the power control room. After several failures, the connection goes through.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Are you there, Comrade Maxim?
There is no response from the other end of the line.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: We must conclude that your attack on this facility and the staff here has some specific purpose or goal. Are you willing to open negotiations?

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: No response. Maybe he's not home?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Comrade, you should be warned that—

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Maxim, we've been to your hideout. We know you were there recently.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We saw things from your childhood there: your belongings, the toys you played with, even your family photos.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A woman there, Tamara, told us your real name is Vanya.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: I recognize your voice, Dr. Vertin, I presume.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: You're wasting your time, and you don't have a lot of that left.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: You're about to get what you deserve—every single one of you drooling lackeys of that hack Sechenov. I'm not going anywhere, so if you're planning to kill me, do it. But it won't stop a damned thing.
The line cuts out.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: This guy's got a death wish. What's he planning?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Whatever it is, he's made it clear where to find him—the power control room.
There's a sudden burst of commotion from the huddle of survivors.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Hey! Alexei! Stay with me, pal! Somebody, please! He needs help!
In a corner, a familiar scientist holds on to his shaking friend.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: I'm here! What's happening?

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: I don't know. He's starting to seize up like the others.

items.speaker: Alexei
items.text: Tie me up. Don't let me ...

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Ah, yeah, got it.
The two men lift the scientist and carry him off into the next room. They've barely left sight before the screams begin.
P-3 returns with a dark, haunted expression; the other scientist follows behind him, sagging low at the shoulders.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Crispy critters! Can't wait to get my hands on that son of a b***h.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Hold things down here for me, will ya, ladies? I'm about to carve a warpath straight to him.

items.speaker: Left & Right
items.text: Comrade Major, before he severed the connection, Maxim warned that killing him would not be sufficient to stop his plans. Perhaps further investigation is needed.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: And what's your big idea? Wait around until all these eggheads crack?

items.speaker: Left & Right
items.text: It remains a matter of critical importance that we determine the nature of their neurological distress.
P-3 stops himself at the doorway, breathing out a long, harsh breath.

items.speaker: Alexei
items.text: Ugh!
The gallery has fallen silent, punctuated sporadically by muffled screams echoing from the scientists tied up in the assembly shop.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Hold on. I think I have a theory.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Go on.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Alexei put on his device a little before I did. So, maybe these things are a kind of ticking time bomb? The longer you wear one, the more likely any little bump will set you off?

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: That could explain why it isn't happening all at once!
X reaches for the THOUGHT Device on his temple. He ponders things for a moment and then lets his hand fall.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: But that means we're all in danger of going off without warning.

items.speaker: X
items.text: That includes me.
The others look to X with newfound concern for their colleague.

items.speaker: X
items.text: There's no reason to think I'm immune. I polymerized myself and installed the device around the same time as they did.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *sigh*

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This wasn't the data we were hoping to collect.
There are harsher words resting on her tongue, but she bites them back.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I know you wanted a deeper understanding of this world, but why did you take such a massive risk? Think about the ramifications. You could lose your mind, or worse, your life.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This is an absolute disaster. I should never have let things get this far.

items.speaker: X
items.text: There's always a method to these things, Mesmer. We aren't finished yet.
X points at his THOUGHT Device.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Progress requires risk. We've always believed that.

items.speaker: X
items.text: As researchers, we discover truth through experimentation. Now, we have one critical piece of the puzzle and the minds to crack it.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Are you suggesting we try to dissect a THOUGHT Device to pinpoint how it causes these psychotic breaks?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Precisely.
The therapist takes a moment to weigh the risk before she agrees.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You're right. There's no use complaining now. We have an opportunity to make the most of the time we have left.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: You're kidding me? We're going to rely on a couple of teenagers to fix this? Nah. F**k that! Back to Plan A. I'm gonna go beat the answers out of Maxim.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Wait, Major, the people here need you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Besides, he already made his intentions clear; he'll die before telling us anything. We have to solve this problem ourselves.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's more, it seems your companion is the only one here with any working knowledge of the THOUGHT Device. We'll need his help.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Someone still needs to get him before he causes more trouble.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then allow me to go. As a neutral party, I might have a better chance to negotiate with him.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Are you insane?

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: This is a life-or-death operation, kid, not a field trip. I'm not about to let you walk out there and get torn apart by those robots.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: We will not let that happen, Comrade Major.
Mesmer Jr. and X have put on hazmat suits and safety goggles borrowed from the assembly room, ready to start the experiment.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I know it may be hard to believe, but we're trained researchers. I was practically raised in the lab.

items.speaker: X
items.text: We may have come here under false pretenses, but we're proven and capable scientists. We can handle this.
Mesmer Jr. and X nod in unison and begin working on the THOUGHT Device.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: I guess that means the summit's back on.
